unsharp.what: Make the picture crisper (or softer) with an unsharp mask.
unsharp.ffmpeg: Sharpen or blur the input video.

options.name: luma_msize_x
options.what: The width of the brightness matrix: an odd number from 3 to 23. The default is 5.

options.name: luma_msize_y
options.what: The height of the brightness matrix: an odd number from 3 to 23. The default is 5.

options.name: luma_amount
options.what: How strongly brightness is sharpened. Reasonable values lie between -1.5 and 1.5: negative values blur, positive values sharpen, 0 does nothing.

options.name: chroma_msize_x
options.what: The width of the colour matrix: an odd number from 3 to 23. The default is 5.

options.name: chroma_msize_y
options.what: The height of the colour matrix: an odd number from 3 to 23. The default is 5.

options.name: chroma_amount
options.what: How strongly the colour planes are sharpened. Reasonable values lie between -1.5 and 1.5.

options.name: alpha_msize_x
options.what: The width of the transparency matrix: an odd number from 3 to 23. The default is 5.

options.name: alpha_msize_y
options.what: The height of the transparency matrix: an odd number from 3 to 23. The default is 5.

options.name: alpha_amount
options.what: How strongly the transparency plane is sharpened. Reasonable values lie between -1.5 and 1.5.

untile.what: Split one tiled picture into a sequence of pictures.
untile.ffmpeg: Untile a frame into a sequence of frames.

options.name: layout
options.what: The grid size, as columns and rows. Default 6x5.

uspp.ffmpeg: Apply Ultra Simple / Slow Post-processing filter.

options.name: quality
options.what: How many levels are used for averaging, from 0 to 8. At 0 the filter has no effect; the default is 3.

options.name: qp
options.what: Forces a constant quantisation parameter, from 0 to 63. If not set, the filter uses the one from the video stream when available.

options.name: use_bframe_qp
options.what: Whether the quantisation parameter of B-frames is used.

options.name: codec
options.what: The codec used instead of the default, snow.

v360.what: Convert 360-degree video between projections, or look into it.

options.name: input
options.what: The projection format of the input video.

options.name: output
options.what: The projection format of the output video.

options.name: interp
options.what: How pixels are interpolated when the projection is converted. More complex methods need much more memory.

options.name: w
options.what: The width of the output video. The default depends on the formats.

options.name: h
options.what: The height of the output video. The default depends on the formats.

options.name: in_stereo
options.what: How the left and right views are laid out in the input video. The default is 2D mono.

options.name: out_stereo
options.what: How the left and right views are laid out in the output video. The default is 2D mono.

options.name: in_forder
options.what: The order of the faces of the input cubemap.

options.name: out_forder
options.what: The order of the faces of the output cubemap.

options.name: in_frot
options.what: The rotation of each face of the input cubemap, as an expression.

options.name: out_frot
options.what: The rotation of each face of the output cubemap, as an expression.

options.name: in_pad
options.what: The padding of the input cubemap faces as a proportion of the face, from 0 to 0.1. 0 means no padding.

options.name: out_pad
options.what: The padding of the output cubemap faces as a proportion of the face, from 0 to 0.1. 0 means no padding.

options.name: fin_pad
options.what: A fixed padding for the input cubemap, from 0 to 100 pixels. If above 0, it overrides the other padding options.

options.name: fout_pad
options.what: A fixed padding for the output cubemap, from 0 to 100 pixels. If above 0, it overrides the other padding options.

options.name: yaw
options.what: The yaw rotation of the output video, from -180 to 180 degrees.

options.name: pitch
options.what: The pitch rotation of the output video, from -180 to 180 degrees.

options.name: roll
options.what: The roll rotation of the output video, from -180 to 180 degrees.

options.name: rorder
options.what: The order in which yaw, pitch and roll are applied to the output video. The default is ypr.

options.name: h_fov
options.what: The horizontal field of view of the output video, from 0 to 360 degrees.

options.name: v_fov
options.what: The vertical field of view of the output video, from 0 to 360 degrees.

options.name: d_fov
options.what: The diagonal field of view of the output video, from 0 to 360 degrees.

options.name: h_flip
options.what: Flips the output video horizontally, swapping left and right.

options.name: v_flip
options.what: Flips the output video vertically, swapping up and down.

options.name: d_flip
options.what: Flips the output video in depth, swapping back and front.

options.name: ih_flip
options.what: Tells the filter that the input video is flipped horizontally.

options.name: iv_flip
options.what: Tells the filter that the input video is flipped vertically.

options.name: in_trans
options.what: Tells the filter that the input video is transposed. Off by default.

options.name: out_trans
options.what: Transposes the output video. Off by default.

options.name: ih_fov
options.what: The horizontal field of view of the input video, from 0 to 360 degrees.

options.name: iv_fov
options.what: The vertical field of view of the input video, from 0 to 360 degrees.

options.name: id_fov
options.what: The diagonal field of view of the input video, from 0 to 360 degrees.

options.name: h_offset
options.what: The horizontal off-axis offset of the output, from -1 to 1. The default is 0.

options.name: v_offset
options.what: The vertical off-axis offset of the output, from -1 to 1. The default is 0.

options.name: alpha_mask
options.what: Builds a mask in the transparency plane by making all unmapped pixels fully transparent. Off by default.

options.name: reset_rot
options.what: Resets the rotation of the output video. Off by default.

vaguedenoiser.what: A wavelet denoiser with several settings.

options.name: threshold
options.what: How strongly the video is filtered; the higher, the more filtered. The default is 2.

options.name: method

choices.name: hard
choices.plain: All values under the threshold will be zeroed

choices.name: soft
choices.plain: Soft: zero below, reduce above threshold

options.what: The filtering method used. Hard thresholding can use a higher threshold than soft before the video looks overfiltered. The default is garrote.

options.name: nsteps
options.what: How many times the wavelet decomposes the picture, from 1 to 32. The default is 6.

options.name: percent
options.what: How much of the full denoising is applied, from 0 to 100. The default is 85.

options.name: planes
options.what: Which colour planes are processed. By default all planes are.

options.name: type
options.what: Which threshold type is used. Universal uses the same threshold for all decompositions; Bayes also depends on each decomposition's coefficients.

varblur.what: A second video says, pixel by pixel, how strong the blur is.

options.name: min_r
options.what: The smallest blur radius allowed, from 0 to 254 (default 0).

options.name: max_r
options.what: The largest blur radius allowed, from 1 to 255 (default 8).

options.name: planes
options.what: A bitmap of which colour planes to process, from 0 to 15 (default 15, all planes).

vectorscope.why: Measurements and diagnostics: they report on the picture, they do not change it
vectorscope.what: Draw the picture's colours on a colour wheel.

options.name: mode
options.what: How the vectorscope is drawn. Default gray.

options.name: x
options.help: set color component on X axis
options.what: Which colour component is shown on the X axis, from 0 to 2. Default 1.

options.name: y
options.help: set color component on Y axis
options.what: Which colour component is shown on the Y axis, from 0 to 2. Default 2.

options.name: intensity
options.what: How much the colour component showing how often each location occurs is brightened, from 0 to 1. Default 0.004.

options.name: envelope
options.what: What kind of envelope is drawn: instant, peak, or both. Default none.

options.name: graticule
options.what: What kind of graticule to draw. Default none.

options.name: opacity
options.what: How opaque the graticule is, from 0 to 1. Default 0.75.

options.name: flags
options.what: What the graticule draws: the white point, the black point, or the point names. Default name.

options.name: bgopacity
options.what: How opaque the background is, from 0 to 1. Default 0.3.

options.name: lthreshold
options.what: Values lower than this are ignored for the colour component not on the X or Y axis, from 0 to 1. Default 0.

options.name: hthreshold
options.what: Values higher than this are ignored for the colour component not on the X or Y axis, from 0 to 1. Default 1.

options.name: colorspace
options.what: The colour space used when drawing the graticule. Default auto.

options.name: tint0
options.what: The colour tint for the gray and tint modes, from -1 to 1. Default 0, which means no tint.

options.name: tint1
options.what: The colour tint for the gray and tint modes, from -1 to 1. Default 0, which means no tint.

vfrdet.why: Measurements and diagnostics: they report on the picture, they do not change it
vfrdet.what: Find out whether the frame rate changes inside the video.

vibrance.what: Boost the dull colours more than the strong ones: a gentler saturation.

options.name: intensity
options.what: The strength of the boost when positive, or of the reduction when negative, from -2 to 2.

options.name: rbal
options.what: The balance of the red channel, from -10 to 10.

options.name: gbal
options.what: The balance of the green channel, from -10 to 10.

options.name: bbal
options.what: The balance of the blue channel, from -10 to 10.

options.name: rlum
options.what: The weight of red in working out brightness, from 0 to 1.

options.name: glum
options.what: The weight of green in working out brightness, from 0 to 1.

options.name: blum
options.what: The weight of blue in working out brightness, from 0 to 1.

options.name: alternate
options.what: When the intensity is negative, change the colours instead of making them less saturated.

options.name: f
options.what: The modulation frequency in Hertz. Default 5 Hz, from 0.1 to 20000.

options.name: d
options.what: The depth of the modulation as a percentage. Default 0.5, from 0 to 1.

vidstabdetect.blocked: Needs two passes over the file: planned with the two-pass encoding.
vidstabdetect.ffmpeg: Extract relative transformations, pass 1 of 2 for stabilization (see vidstabtransform for pass 2).

options.name: result
options.help: path to the file used to write the transforms
options.what: The path of the file the transforms information is written to. The default is transforms.trf.

options.name: shakiness
options.help: how shaky is the video and how quick is the camera? 1: little (fast) 10: very strong/quick (slow)
options.what: How shaky the video is and how quick the camera is, from 1 (little) to 10 (strong). The default is 5.

options.name: accuracy
options.what: The accuracy of the detection, from 1 (low) to 15 (high). The default is 15.

options.name: stepsize
options.help: region around minimum is scanned with 1 pixel resolution
options.what: The step size of the search; the region around the minimum is scanned with 1 pixel resolution. From 1 to 32.

options.name: mincontrast
options.help: below this contrast a field is discarded (0-1)
options.what: Below this contrast a local measurement field is discarded, from 0 to 1.

options.name: show
options.help: 0: draw nothing; 1,2: show fields and transforms
options.what: Shows fields and transforms in the resulting frames, from 0 to 2. 0 disables any visualisation.

options.name: tripod
options.help: virtual tripod mode (if >0): motion is compared to a reference reference frame (frame # is the value)
options.what: The reference frame number for tripod mode, counted from 1. Motion is compared to that frame to keep the view absolutely still; 0 disables it.

options.name: fileformat
options.what: The format of the transforms data file. Binary is roughly 40% smaller than ASCII.

vidstabtransform.blocked: Needs the first pass: planned with the two-pass encoding.
vidstabtransform.ffmpeg: Transform the frames, pass 2 of 2 for stabilization (see vidstabdetect for pass 1).

options.name: input
options.help: set path to the file storing the transforms
options.what: The path of the file the transforms are read from. The default is transforms.trf.

options.name: smoothing
options.help: set number of frames*2 + 1 used for lowpass filtering
options.what: The number of frames used to smooth the camera movement is this value times 2, plus 1, in the past and future. A larger value gives a smoother video but limits camera pans and tilts; 0 simulates a static camera.

options.name: optalgo
options.what: The algorithm that optimises the camera path.

options.name: maxshift
options.help: set maximal number of pixels to translate image
options.what: The largest number of pixels frames are translated by. -1 means no limit.

options.name: maxangle
options.help: set maximal angle in rad to rotate image
options.what: The largest angle frames are rotated by, in radians. -1 means no limit.

options.name: crop
options.what: How borders that become visible through movement compensation are dealt with.

options.name: invert
options.what: Inverts the transforms if set to 1. The default is 0.

options.name: relative
options.what: Treats the transforms as relative to the previous frame if 1, or absolute if 0.

options.name: zoom
options.help: set percentage to zoom (>0: zoom in, <0: zoom out
options.what: The zoom percentage, from -100 to 100. A positive value zooms in, a negative value zooms out; 0 is no zoom.

options.name: optzoom
options.help: set optimal zoom (0: nothing, 1: optimal static zoom, 2: optimal dynamic zoom)
options.what: Sets optimal zooming to avoid borders, from 0 to 2. The Zoom value is added to the one calculated here.

options.name: zoomspeed
options.help: for adative zoom: percent to zoom maximally each frame
options.what: The most the zoom may change each frame, in percent, from 0 to 5. Used when automatic zoom is 2.

options.name: interpol
options.what: The type of interpolation used.

options.name: tripod
options.help: enable virtual tripod mode (same as relative=0:smoothing=0)
options.what: Enables virtual tripod mode, equivalent to relative=0 and smoothing=0. Also use the tripod option of the first pass.

options.name: debug
options.help: enable debug mode and writer global motions information to file
options.what: Increases log verbosity and writes the detected global motions to the temporary file global_motions.trf.

vif.why: Measurements between two videos: they compare, they do not change the picture
vif.ffmpeg: Calculate the VIF between two video streams.
vif.what: Score the visual information fidelity of two videos.

vignette.what: Darken the corners, as old lenses and films do.
vignette.ffmpeg: Make or reverse a vignette effect.

options.name: angle
options.what: The angle of the simulated lens, in radians, as a number or an expression. It is limited to 0 to PI/2. The default is PI/5.

options.name: x0
options.help: set circle center position on x-axis
options.what: The horizontal position of the centre of the circle, as an expression. The default is w/2.

options.name: y0
options.help: set circle center position on y-axis
options.what: The vertical position of the centre of the circle, as an expression. The default is h/2.

options.name: mode
options.what: Whether the edges get darker or brighter.

options.name: eval
options.what: When the expressions (angle and centre) are worked out.

options.name: dither
options.what: Dither the result to reduce the circular banding. On by default.

options.name: aspect
options.what: The aspect ratio of the vignette. Setting it to the pixel aspect ratio of the input gives a rectangular vignette that follows the picture.

virtualbass.what: Make small speakers seem to play deeper notes.

options.name: cutoff
options.what: The cut-off frequency of the virtual bass. Default 250 Hz, from 100 to 500.

options.name: strength
options.what: How strong the virtual bass is. Default 3, from 0.5 to 3.

vmafmotion.why: Measurements and diagnostics: they report on the picture, they do not change it
vmafmotion.what: Measure how much the picture moves, as VMAF does.

options.name: stats_file
options.help: Set file where to store per-frame difference information
options.what: If set, the motion score of each frame compared with the previous frame is saved to this file. A file name of - sends the data to standard output.

volume.what: Make the sound louder or quieter.

options.name: volume
options.what: The volume adjustment, as a number or an expression. Default 1.0.

options.name: precision
options.what: The mathematical precision of the volume scaling; it decides which input sample formats are allowed. Default is float.

options.name: eval
options.what: Whether the volume expression is evaluated once (at start or when the volume command is sent) or for each incoming frame. Default is once.

options.name: replaygain
options.help: Apply replaygain side data when present

choices.name: drop
choices.plain: Remove ReplayGain side data, ignoring its contents (the default)

choices.name: ignore
choices.plain: Ignore ReplayGain side data, but leave it in the frame

choices.name: track
choices.plain: Prefer the track gain, if present

choices.name: album
choices.plain: Prefer the album gain, if present

options.what: What to do with ReplayGain side data found in the input: drop it, ignore it but keep it, or prefer the track or album gain. Default is drop.

options.name: replaygain_preamp
options.what: A pre-amplification in dB applied to the selected ReplayGain gain. Default 0, from -15 to 15.

options.name: replaygain_noclip
options.what: Prevents clipping by limiting the gain applied. On by default.

volumedetect.what: Report the mean and peak level.

builtin.audio-converter: Volume: normalise to a peak (the measurement)

vpp_amf.ffmpeg: AMF video scaling and format conversion
vpp_amf.what: Scaling and format conversion on an AMD card.

options.name: w
options.what: The width of the output video, as an expression like in the scale filter. Default is the input width.

options.name: h
options.what: The height of the output video, as an expression like in the scale filter. Default is the input height.

options.name: format
options.what: The pixel format of the output; by default the input format is used.

options.name: scale_type
options.what: The algorithm used for scaling, bilinear or bicubic. The default is bilinear.

options.name: color_profile
options.what: Sets all colour properties at once: BT.601, BT.709 or BT.2020.

options.name: in_color_range
options.what: Overrides the colour range of the input, studio or full.

options.name: out_color_range
options.what: The colour range of the output, studio (restricted) or full.

options.name: in_primaries
options.what: Overrides the colour primaries of the input.

options.name: out_primaries
options.what: The colour primaries of the output.

options.name: in_trc
options.what: Overrides the transfer characteristics of the input.

options.name: out_trc
options.what: The transfer characteristics of the output.

options.name: force_original_aspect_ratio
options.help: decrease or increase w/h if necessary to keep the original AR
options.what: Whether the width or height is decreased or increased where needed to keep the original aspect ratio. Works like the scale filter option.

options.name: force_divisible_by
options.help: enforce that the output resolution is divisible by a defined integer when force_original_aspect_ratio is used
options.what: Makes the output size divisible by this whole number when the original aspect ratio is being kept. 1 to 256, default 1.

options.name: reset_sar
options.help: reset SAR to 1 and scale to square pixels if scaling proportionally
options.what: Whether the pixel shape is reset to square pixels when scaling proportionally. Off by default.

vpp_qsv.plain: Resize and convert on Intel Quick Sync
vpp_qsv.what: Scaling and format conversion on the Intel graphics chip.

options.name: deinterlace
options.what: Which deinterlace mode is used: off, bob or advanced. Default is off.

options.name: denoise
options.what: How strongly noise is removed. 0 to 100, default 0.

options.name: detail
options.what: How strongly detail is enhanced. 0 to 100, default 0.

options.name: framerate
options.what: The frame rate of the output video.

options.name: procamp
options.what: Turns the ProcAmp (hue, saturation, contrast, brightness) adjustments on or off. 0 or 1, default 0.

options.name: hue
options.what: The ProcAmp hue adjustment. -180 to 180, default 0.

options.name: saturation
options.what: The ProcAmp saturation adjustment. 0 to 10, default 1.

options.name: contrast
options.what: The ProcAmp contrast adjustment. 0 to 10, default 1.

options.name: brightness
options.what: The ProcAmp brightness adjustment. -100 to 100, default 0.

options.name: transpose
options.what: How the picture is rotated or flipped.

options.name: cw
options.help: set the width crop area expression
options.what: The width of the crop area, as an expression. Default is the input width.

options.name: ch
options.help: set the height crop area expression
options.what: The height of the crop area, as an expression. Default is the input height.

options.name: cx
options.help: set the x crop area expression
options.what: The horizontal position of the crop area, as an expression. Default centres it.

options.name: cy
options.help: set the y crop area expression
options.what: The vertical position of the crop area, as an expression. Default centres it.

options.name: w
options.help: Output video width(0=input video width, -1=keep input video aspect)

options.name: width
options.help: Output video width(0=input video width, -1=keep input video aspect)
options.what: The width of the output video; 0 uses the input width and -1 keeps the input aspect. Default is the crop width.

options.name: h
options.help: Output video height(0=input video height, -1=keep input video aspect)

options.name: height
options.help: Output video height(0=input video height, -1=keep input video aspect)
options.what: The height of the output video; 0 uses the input height and -1 keeps the input aspect. Default follows the crop proportions.

options.name: format
options.what: The pixel format of the output. Default is the same as the input.

options.name: async_depth
options.help: Internal parallelization depth, the higher the value the higher the latency.
options.what: The internal parallelization depth; the higher the value, the higher the latency. Default 4.

options.name: scale_mode
options.help: scaling & format conversion mode (mode compute(3), vd(4) and ve(5) are only available on some platforms)
options.what: The scaling and format conversion mode; compute, vd and ve are only available on some platforms.

options.name: rate
options.help: Generate output at frame rate or field rate, available only for deinterlace mode

choices.name: frame
choices.help: Output at frame rate (one frame of output for each field-pair)
choices.plain: Frame rate (one frame per field pair)

choices.name: field
choices.help: Output at field rate (one frame of output for each field)

options.what: Whether output is at frame rate or field rate; only available for deinterlace mode. The default is frame.

options.name: out_range
options.what: Whether the output uses the full or the limited colour range.

options.name: out_color_matrix
options.what: The colour matrix coefficient set of the output.

options.name: out_color_primaries
options.what: The colour primaries of the output.

options.name: out_color_transfer
options.what: The colour transfer characteristics of the output.

options.name: tonemap
options.help: Perform tonemapping (0=disable tonemapping, 1=perform tonemapping if the input has HDR metadata)
options.what: Whether tone mapping is done when the input has HDR metadata. 0 turns it off, 1 turns it on. Default 0.

vsrc_amf.what: Record the screen with an AMD card.

options.name: monitor_index
options.help: Index of display monitor to capture
options.what: Which display monitor is captured. 0 to 8, default 0.

options.name: framerate
options.what: The frame rate of the capture. Default 60.

options.name: duplicate_output
options.help: Use display output duplication for screen capture
options.what: Whether display output duplication is used for the screen capture. On by default.

options.name: capture_mode

choices.name: keep_framerate
choices.help: Capture component maintains the frame rate

choices.name: wait_for_present
choices.help: Capture component waits for flip (present) event

options.what: How the capture is synchronised: keep the frame rate, wait for the flip (present) event, or return the current visible surface straight away. The default is keep_framerate.

vstack.what: Place two or more videos above each other.

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many input videos are stacked one above the other (default 2).

options.name: shortest
options.help: force termination when the shortest input terminates
options.what: Ends the output when the shortest input ends (default off).

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many videos are stacked on top of each other. 2 to 65535, default 2.

options.name: shortest
options.help: Force termination when the shortest input terminates
options.what: Whether the output ends when the shortest input ends.

options.name: width
options.help: Set output width (0 to use the width of input 0)
options.what: The width of the stacked output; 0 uses the width of the first input. Default 0.

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many videos are stacked on top of each other. 2 to 65535, default 2.

options.name: shortest
options.help: Force termination when the shortest input terminates
options.what: Whether the output ends when the shortest input ends.

options.name: width
options.help: Set output width (0 to use the width of input 0)
options.what: The width of the stacked output; 0 uses the width of the first input. Default 0.

w3fdif.what: A deinterlacer using three fields.
w3fdif.ffmpeg: Apply Martin Weston three field deinterlace.

options.name: filter
options.what: Which set of interlacing filter coefficients is used. The default is complex.

options.name: mode

choices.name: frame
choices.help: send one frame for each frame

choices.name: field
choices.help: send one frame for each field

options.what: Whether one frame is output for each frame or for each field. The default is field.

options.name: parity
options.help: specify the assumed picture field parity
options.what: The field parity assumed for the interlaced input. If it is unknown, top field first is assumed.

options.name: deint

choices.name: interlaced
choices.help: only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced

options.what: Which frames are deinterlaced. The default is all.

waveform.why: Measurements and diagnostics: they report on the picture, they do not change it
waveform.what: Draw brightness against position like a studio waveform monitor.

options.name: mode
options.what: Whether the graph is drawn per row or per column. Default column.

options.name: intensity
options.what: How bright the plotted values are, from 0 to 1. Default 0.04. Smaller values show how many equal values are spread across rows or columns.

options.name: mirror
options.what: Whether higher values are shown on the left in row mode and at the top in column mode. On by default.

options.name: display
options.what: How the graphs of the colour components are laid out. Default stack.

options.name: components
options.what: Which colour components to display, from 1 to 15. Default 1, which means only brightness or red for RGB.

options.name: envelope
options.what: What kind of envelope is drawn. Default none.

options.name: filter
options.what: How the colour components are filtered and shown. Default lowpass.

options.name: graticule

choices.name: green
choices.plain: Display green graticule showing legal broadcast ranges

choices.name: orange
choices.plain: Display orange graticule showing legal broadcast ranges

choices.name: invert
choices.plain: Display invert graticule showing legal broadcast ranges

options.what: Which graticule to display, showing legal broadcast ranges. Default none.

options.name: opacity
options.what: How opaque the graticule is, from 0 to 1. Default 0.75.

options.name: flags
options.what: What the graticule draws: numbers above the lines, or dots instead of lines. Default numbers.

options.name: scale
options.what: The scale used for the graticule. Default digital.

options.name: bgopacity
options.what: How opaque the background is, from 0 to 1. Default 0.75.

options.name: tint0
options.what: The tint of the output, from -1 to 1. Only used with the lowpass filter, when the display is not overlay and the input is not RGB.

options.name: tint1
options.what: The tint of the output, from -1 to 1. Only used with the lowpass filter, when the display is not overlay and the input is not RGB.

options.name: fitmode
options.what: How the pixel shape of the output is set so the waveform is not stretched too much in one direction. Default none.

options.name: input

choices.name: all
choices.help: try to select from all available formats

options.what: Whether the filter picks from all available input formats or the first available one. Default first.

weave.what: Put pairs of fields back together into frames.
weave.ffmpeg: Weave input video fields into frames.

options.name: first_field
options.what: Which field is placed first when fields are woven into frames.

xbr.what: Enlarge pixel art by 2, 3 or 4 with the xBR method.
xbr.ffmpeg: Scale the input using xBR algorithm.

options.name: n
options.what: The scaling dimension, from 2 to 4: 2 for 2xBR, 3 for 3xBR, 4 for 4xBR. The default is 3.

xcorrelate.what: Compare a video with shifted copies of another.
xcorrelate.ffmpeg: Cross-correlate first video stream with second video stream.

options.name: planes
options.what: A bitmap of which colour planes to process, from 0 to 15 (default 7).

options.name: secondary

choices.name: first
choices.help: process only first secondary frame, ignore rest

options.what: Whether only the first frame of the second video is used, or every frame (default all).

xfade.what: Dissolve, wipe or slide from the end of one video into the start of the next.
xfade.ffmpeg: Cross fade one video with another video.

options.name: transition
options.what: Which cross-fade effect is used (default fade).

options.name: duration
options.what: How long the cross fade lasts, from 0 to 60 seconds (default 1).

options.name: offset
options.help: set cross fade start relative to first input stream
options.what: When the cross fade starts, relative to the first input (default 0).

options.name: expr
options.what: A formula that defines the custom transition effect.

xmedian.what: Keep the middle value of each pixel across several videos: removes anything that moves.
xmedian.ffmpeg: Pick median pixels from several video inputs.

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many input videos are used, from 3 to 255 (default 3); with an even number the result is the mean of the two middle values.

options.name: planes
options.what: A bitmap of which colour planes to filter, from 0 to 15 (default 15, all planes).

options.name: percentile
options.what: Which value is picked: 0.5 picks the median, 0 the minimum and 1 the maximum (default 0.5).

xpsnr.why: Measurements between two videos: they compare, they do not change the picture
xpsnr.ffmpeg: Calculate the extended perceptually weighted peak signal-to-noise ratio (XPSNR) between two video streams.
xpsnr.what: Score a video against its original with a perception-weighted PSNR.

options.name: stats_file
options.help: Set file where to store per-frame XPSNR information
options.what: If set, the XPSNR value of each frame and colour plane is saved to this file. A file name of - sends the data to standard output.

xstack.what: Place several videos in a grid you describe.
xstack.ffmpeg: Stack video inputs into custom layout.

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many input videos are stacked (default 2).

options.name: layout
options.what: Where each input sits in the output, inputs separated by '|', each given as column_row; you must set it yourself.

options.name: grid
options.what: Arranges the inputs in a grid of COLUMNSxROWS; there must be exactly that many input videos.

options.name: shortest
options.help: force termination when the shortest input terminates
options.what: Ends the output when the shortest input ends (default off).

options.name: fill
options.help: set the color for unused pixels
options.what: The colour that fills any unused pixels; by default it is none, which turns filling off.

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many videos are stacked into the layout. 2 to 65535, default 2.

options.name: shortest
options.help: Force termination when the shortest input terminates
options.what: Whether the output ends when the shortest input ends.

options.name: layout
options.what: Where each input goes in the output; it also lets you give an output size for each input.

options.name: grid
options.what: A fixed grid layout, given as a size.

options.name: grid_tile_size
options.help: set tile size in grid layout
options.what: The output size of each input when a grid is set; if unset, the size of the first input is used.

options.name: fill
options.help: Set the color for unused pixels
options.what: The colour used for pixels no input covers.

options.name: inputs
options.what: How many videos are stacked into the layout. 2 to 65535, default 2.

options.name: shortest
options.help: Force termination when the shortest input terminates
options.what: Whether the output ends when the shortest input ends.

options.name: layout
options.what: Where each input goes in the output; it also lets you give an output size for each input.

options.name: grid
options.what: A fixed grid layout, given as a size.

options.name: grid_tile_size
options.help: set tile size in grid layout
options.what: The output size of each input when a grid is set; if unset, the size of the first input is used.

options.name: fill
options.help: Set the color for unused pixels
options.what: The colour used for pixels no input covers.

yadif.what: Remove the comb pattern that interlaced video shows on moving things.

options.name: mode

choices.name: send_frame
choices.help: send one frame for each frame

choices.name: send_field
choices.help: send one frame for each field
choices.plain: One picture per field (doubles the frame rate)

choices.name: send_frame_nospatial
choices.help: send one frame for each frame, but skip spatial interlacing check
choices.plain: One picture per frame, skip the spatial check

choices.name: send_field_nospatial
choices.help: send one frame for each field, but skip spatial interlacing check
choices.plain: One picture per field, skip the spatial check

options.what: One picture per frame, or one per field, which doubles the frame rate.

options.name: parity
options.help: specify the assumed picture field parity
options.what: Which field of an interlaced frame comes first. Auto detects it.

options.name: deint

choices.name: interlaced
choices.help: only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced

options.what: Treat every frame, or only the frames marked as interlaced.

options.name: mode

choices.name: send_frame
choices.help: send one frame for each frame

choices.name: send_field
choices.help: send one frame for each field

choices.name: send_frame_nospatial
choices.help: send one frame for each frame, but skip spatial interlacing check
choices.plain: One frame per frame, no spatial check

choices.name: send_field_nospatial
choices.help: send one frame for each field, but skip spatial interlacing check
choices.plain: One frame per field, no spatial check

options.what: Whether one frame is output for each frame or for each field, with or without the spatial interlacing check. The default is send_frame.

options.name: parity
options.help: specify the assumed picture field parity
options.what: Which field of the interlaced input is assumed to come first; automatic detection is the default, and if unknown, top field first is assumed.

options.name: deint

choices.name: interlaced
choices.help: only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced
choices.plain: Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced

options.what: Whether all frames are deinterlaced or only those marked as interlaced. The default is all.

yaepblur.what: Another blur that keeps the outlines sharp.
yaepblur.ffmpeg: Yet another edge preserving blur filter.

options.name: radius
options.what: The radius of the window used for blurring. The default is 3.

options.name: planes
options.what: Which colour planes are filtered. By default only the first plane is.

options.name: sigma
options.what: How strongly the picture is blurred. The default is 128.

yuvtestsrc.why: Pictures made out of nothing: test patterns, colour bars and generated art, with no video to apply them to
yuvtestsrc.what: A test picture of YUV colours.

options.name: size
options.what: The size of the generated video. Default 320x240.

options.name: rate
options.what: The number of frames per second. Default 25.

options.name: duration
options.what: The length of the generated video.

options.name: sar
options.what: The sample aspect ratio, the shape of each pixel, of the video. Default 1/1.

zmq.why: Internal plumbing: they change how ffmpeg handles the picture, not what it looks like
zmq.ffmpeg: Receive commands through ZMQ and broker them to filters.
zmq.plain: Receive commands over a network socket
zmq.what: Let another program change filter settings while it runs.

options.name: bind_address
options.what: The network address the filter listens on for commands. Default tcp://*:5555.

zoneplate.why: Pictures made out of nothing: test patterns, colour bars and generated art, with no video to apply them to
zoneplate.what: The circular test pattern used to check lenses and scalers.

options.name: size
options.what: The size of the generated frames. Default 320x240.

options.name: rate
options.what: The number of frames per second. Default 25.

options.name: duration
options.what: The length of the generated video. If not set or negative, the video is generated forever.

options.name: sar
options.what: The sample aspect ratio, the shape of each pixel, of the video. Default 1/1.

options.name: precision
options.what: The precision in bits of the look-up table used for sine calculations, from 4 to 16. Default 10.

options.name: xo
options.what: The horizontal axis offset of the output signal. Default 0.

options.name: yo
options.what: The vertical axis offset of the output signal. Default 0.

options.name: to
options.what: The time axis offset of the output signal. Default 0.

options.name: k0
options.what: A constant added to the signal phase (0-order). Default 0.

options.name: kx
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the horizontal axis (1-order). Default 0.

options.name: ky
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the vertical axis (1-order). Default 0.

options.name: kt
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the time axis (1-order). Default 0.

options.name: kxt
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the combination of horizontal and time axes. Default 0.

options.name: kyt
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the combination of vertical and time axes. Default 0.

options.name: kxy
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the combination of horizontal and vertical axes. Default 0.

options.name: kx2
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the horizontal axis (2-order). Default 0.

options.name: ky2
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the vertical axis (2-order). Default 0.

options.name: kt2
options.what: The phase factor multiplier for the time axis (2-order). Default 0.

options.name: ku
options.what: A constant added to the final phase to make the chroma-blue component of the signal. Default 0.

options.name: kv
options.what: A constant added to the final phase to make the chroma-red component of the signal. Default 0.

zoompan.what: Slowly zoom into or across the picture. Made for stills: on video it needs care.

options.name: zoom
options.what: The zoom level, as a number or an expression. The range is 1 to 10; the default is 1.

options.name: x
options.what: The x position of the view, as a number or an expression.

options.name: y
options.what: The y position of the view, as a number or an expression.

options.name: d
options.what: For how many frames the effect lasts for a single input image, as a number or an expression. The default is 90.

options.name: s
options.what: The size of the output image. The default is hd720.

options.name: fps
options.what: The frame rate of the output. The default is 25.

zscale.ffmpeg: Apply resizing, colorspace and bit depth conversion.
zscale.plain: Resize with colour-space control
zscale.what: A resizer that also converts the colour space and bit depth.

options.name: width
options.what: The output width, as a number or an expression. By default the input width; 0 also means the input width.

options.name: height
options.what: The output height, as a number or an expression. By default the input height; 0 also means the input height.

options.name: size
options.what: The output width and height together, written like 1280x720.

options.name: dither
options.what: The kind of dithering used.

options.name: filter
options.what: Which filter is used to resize.

options.name: out_range
options.what: The colour range of the output. By default the same as the input.

options.name: primaries
options.what: The colour primaries of the output. By default the same as the input.

options.name: transfer
options.what: The transfer characteristics of the output. By default the same as the input.

options.name: matrix
options.what: The colourspace matrix of the output. By default the same as the input.

options.name: in_range
options.what: The colour range of the input. By default detected.

options.name: primariesin
options.what: The colour primaries of the input. By default detected.

options.name: transferin
options.what: The transfer characteristics of the input. By default detected.

options.name: matrixin
options.what: The colourspace matrix of the input. By default detected.

options.name: chromal
options.what: The chroma location of the output.

options.name: chromalin
options.what: The chroma location of the input.

options.name: npl
options.what: The nominal peak luminance.

options.name: agamma
options.what: Allow an approximation of the gamma curve.

options.name: param_a
options.help: parameter A, which is parameter "b" for bicubic, and the number of filter taps for lanczos
options.what: Parameter A of the scaling filter: "b" for bicubic, the number of filter taps for lanczos.

options.name: param_b
options.help: parameter B, which is parameter "c" for bicubic
options.what: Parameter B of the scaling filter: "c" for bicubic.

turn.what: Rotate the picture a quarter or a half turn, for a video shot with the phone on its side.

crop-edges.what: Cut a strip off each edge of the picture.
crop-edges.note: How much can be cut depends on the size of each video, so the formula clamps: whatever the numbers, at least 2 px of picture stay.

blurfit.what: Fit the picture inside a frame of another shape, and fill the rest with a blurred, enlarged copy of itself.

play-backwards.what: Run the clip from its end to its start, sound included. The whole clip is held in memory.

text.what: Write a line of text on the picture. It can show the file's name and the time played or left.

watermark.what: Put a picture, a logo for example, in a corner.

burn-subtitles.what: Draw the first subtitle track of the file into the picture. The output then has no subtitle track. Works with text subtitles only.

channels.what: Swap left and right, play one channel on both sides, or mix both into one.

equalizer.what: A gain for each octave band, from 31 Hz to 16 kHz.

compressor.what: Everything above a level is lowered by a ratio, so the loud and the quiet parts get closer.

fade-in.what: Raise the sound from silence over the first moments.

fade-out.what: Lower the sound to silence over the last moments.

trim-silence.what: Cut the silence before the sound starts and after it stops - never silence inside the song.

keep-range.what: Keep only the part between two times, counted on what the effects above it left.

limit-duration.what: Keep at most this many seconds from the start.

volume-loudness.what: Bring the loudness of the part that is kept to a target, with a limiter so the gain cannot clip.

volume-peak.what: Bring the highest sample to a target level.

volume-replaygain.what: Apply the ReplayGain gain of the track (or of the album) to the sound itself, with a limiter.

builtin.audio-converter: Volume: ReplayGain, and the ReplayGain tags

volume-gain.what: Make the sound louder or quieter by a fixed amount, with a limiter.

silence-end.what: Cut the song where its trailing silence begins and leave exactly this much silence after it, so an LP plays as separate tracks.

controls.label: Keep a little of the old tail

replaygain-tags.what: Write the track gain and peak of the new file as tags; the sound is untouched.
